title: Sylvester Rice and Adolphus Osbrooke
summary: Jones calls Sylvester Rice the best all-around drummer and conductor, who left New York disgusted for the Midwest.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yes. Like I started on trumpet and how I wound up. I don't know what I'm doing. I have to ask all of these peoples; but my knowledge of the musical instruments and with my experience - and when I say my experience I'm not speaking Jo Jones first-person singular. I'm speaking Jo Jones fifth-person plurally. All these peoples we realize - I remember at the time. Now the greatest all around drummer that I remember as a conductor and everything was a fellow by the name of Sylvester Rice. I have never seen nobody with the exception of Mr. Billy Gladstone that played in Radio City, that could conduct any symphony. He could conduct everything, Sylvester Rice.
Who did he play with, Jo?

He played with his father's band, Eli Rice. It was a Midwestern band. Nobody could ever top him. He came in New York for a moment, he was disgusted, and went back out to the Midwest because they didn't have his knowledge. He was disgusted because they were too slow in thinking. He rehearsed with everything that they had here and they had no music for him. He was like Adolphus Osbrooke. They didn't have nothing here.
Adolphus Osbrooke was a great bass player, O Osbrooke (Jo)
He's a genius, you know that.
He's been writing for Lawrence Welk and what not.
